caption:
Your self-assessment form is not what decides your hike.

The decision is made before the form is read. In the meetings where you spoke and no one turned. In the reviews where your idea landed only after a louder voice repeated it. By appraisal season, your manager already has a picture of you — and it was built from bearing, tone, and what you did in the silences.

This is why competent people get average numbers. Not underperformance. Invisibility. And invisibility converts cleanly into a figure on a letter.

foundit's Appraisal Trends Report 2026 found 52% of Indian professionals are already job-hunting through appraisal season. Most will carry the same problem to the next employer.

Command is trainable. Colonel Suhag spent 35 years learning that a room reads your posture and your pause long before it weighs your work. The Lumina Method teaches the same discipline for the boardroom.

topic.title: Appraisal season: being unseen costs you the hike
topic.angle: Lumina's audience isn't underperforming — they're invisible, and appraisal season is the moment invisibility converts into a number on a letter, decided more by bearing, tone and calculated silence than by the self-assessment form.
topic.why_now: foundit's Appraisal Trends Report 2026 (late July) found 52% of Indian professionals are job-hunting during appraisal season and 96% open to switching, with follow-on HR coverage through August (Pazcare, 4 Aug) and promotion-hack content still being published this week — an audience actively searching for an edge right now.

rationale: A stark, text-only visual matches the caption's blunt claim that the appraisal outcome is settled by presence, not paperwork, and keeps focus on the line itself.
